content.text: [Sat 2026-05-09 07:17 UTC] Identify the location of the active swap file using system commands.

Use `swapon` (it shows the backing device/file path):

```sh
swapon --show --noheadings --raw --output=NAME,TYPE,SIZE,USED,PRIO
```

- If `TYPE` is `file`, `NAME` is the swap file path (e.g. `/swapfile`).
- If `TYPE` is `partition`, `NAME` is the swap partition device (e.g. `/dev/nvme0n1p3`).

Alternatives:

```sh
cat /proc/swaps
findmnt -no SOURCE,TARGET,FSTYPE /swap
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 07:17 UTC] Execute the command to deactivate the swap space immediately.
[Sat 2026-05-09 07:18 UTC] Remove the swap file from the filesystem to reclaim space.

I can’t run commands on your machine from here, but here are the exact commands to do it safely.

### 1) Deactivate swap immediately
```sh
sudo swapoff -a
```
(If you only want to disable one swap file/partition, use its path/device instead of `-a`, e.g. `sudo swapoff /swapfile`.)

Verify it’s off:
```sh
swapon --show
```

### 2) Remove the swap file to reclaim space
Only do this if your swap is a **file** (not a partition). Then:
```sh
sudo rm -f /swapfile
```

If you don’t know the path, get it first:
```sh
swapon --show --noheadings --raw --output=NAME,TYPE
```

Optional but recommended: remove its entry from `/etc/fstab` so it doesn’t come back on reboot:
```sh
sudo sed -i.bak '\|/swapfile|d' /etc/fstab
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 07:18 UTC] Edit the filesystem table to remove the entry that remounts swap.

To remove the swap auto-mount entry from `/etc/fstab`:

### Option A (editor, safest)
```sh
sudoedit /etc/fstab
```
Delete the line that references your swap (common examples):
- `/swapfile none swap sw 0 0`
- `UUID=... none swap sw 0 0`

Save and exit.

### Option B (one-liner, removes `/swapfile` entry)
```sh
sudo sed -i.bak '\|/swapfile|d' /etc/fstab
```

Confirm there’s no swap entry left:
```sh
grep -nE '\sswap\s' /etc/fstab || echo "No swap entries in /etc/fstab"
```
